//: AUTONOMOUS permissions — OPT-IN ONLY. ⚠️ Read all of this before applying.
Applied only by `./install.sh --autonomous`, which requires you to type a
confirmation. It is never applied by a plain install, and it is never a
default: someone else's configuration is not a template for yours.
WHAT IT DOES: grants Bash(*) under defaultMode 'auto', so almost no command
prompts. Combined with the baseline's deny and ask rules, which still apply.
WHAT YOU ARE ACCEPTING: under auto mode the blanket Bash(*) grant is dropped,
so a Bash command no surviving rule matches goes to Claude Code's classifier.
`claude-danger-guard` runs ahead of that as a deterministic first layer. It is
NOT the only boundary in auto mode, but a command a narrow allow rule covers
(including anything saved by 'don't ask again') gets no semantic review.
Outside auto mode (default, acceptEdits) Bash(*) is live and the guard IS the
only shape check on shell access. The guard blocks a specific set of destructive SHAPES —
sudo, curl piped to a shell, force pushes, raw disk writes, credential reads,
and any rm pointing outside your workspace. Everything it does not positively
recognise as dangerous, it ALLOWS, because a guard that misfires on ordinary
work gets disabled and a disabled guard protects nothing. So the set of things
that can still go wrong is large: overwriting a file you needed, a bad sed
across a repo, an API call with real consequences, a git operation that loses
uncommitted work.
THE TRADE THIS ASSUMES: a wide grant is only safe alongside a STRONGER
obligation to stop at decision gates. If Claude may act without asking, then
it must reliably stop before anything hard to reverse or outward-facing. That
obligation lives in the toolkit policy, not here — see its policy/CLAUDE.md,
Gate at decisions section. Applying this file without that contract loaded is the
actual mistake, not the permissions themselves.
BEFORE YOU APPLY IT, be able to answer:
- What does the guard NOT catch in my environment?
- What here is irreversible, and what has no backup?
- What are my decision gates, written down where Claude will read them?
TO REVERSE: delete the `Bash(*)` entry from `permissions.allow` and remove
`defaultMode` in ~/.claude/settings.json. install.sh keeps a .bak.
